newsitem.title: UK: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.1 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.1 pct in Sept.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following retail price indices for July:
RETAIL PRICES INDEX SEPT AUG SEPT 95
Mth pct change ex MIPs, tax 0.6 0.7 0.5
COMPONENT DETAILS OF THE ALL-ITEMS INDEX (PCT CHANGES) -
NOTE - Consensus forecast was RPI +0.4 pct MM,+2.0 pct YY, RPIX +2.8 pct YY, RPIY +2.4 pct YY.

The ONS said food prices caused the largest downward effect on the 12-month rate, though there were also downward effects from housing costs and household goods' prices. The major upward effects on the 12-month rate came from motoring costs, clothing and footwear prices and from household services' prices.
The 5.2 percent increase in clothing and footwear prices was the largest monthly rise since records began in 1947, the ONS said. That reflects a very strong recovery from the summer sales.
The increase in motoring costs was largely down to higher petrol prices.
The ONS said for October, seasonal food prices have tended to rise, although last year was an exception. The major supermarket chains look set to continue with their price war in October, it said.
Extra duties on cider, announced in last year's budget, take effect in October.
Last October saw a reduction in mortgage interest rates, which will fall out of the year-on-year equation. That could add 0.2 percentage points to the year-on-year rate in October.
British Telecommunications Plc will introduce further cuts in the cost of certain telephone calls, the ONS said.
Petrol prices look set to continue rising as higher crude oil prices feed through. Domestic heating oil prices could also rise for that reason.
Motoring insurance prices could also rise, the ONS said.
